question.text: A close-ended Cat III AIF (e.g., Vindhya Event-Driven Fund launched for 5 years with a 2-year lock-in) has which of the following redemption characteristics?

answer.text: Investors can redeem freely at daily NAV from day one
Investors cannot redeem during the lock-in; after the lock-in, redemptions may be permitted with an exit load as specified in the PPM, until the fund tenure expires
Investors can redeem only if SEBI issues a specific approval for each exit
Investors are entitled to unrestricted quarterly redemption at any time

explanation.text: The Logic: Close-ended AIFs have redemption restrictions: investors cannot redeem during the PPM-specified lock-in, and unrestricted redemption is not available before tenure expiry or winding-up. After lock-in, redemptions may be permitted on terms (including exit load) specified in the PPM. The Trap: Option A describes open-ended Cat III. Option C is fabricated. Option D overstates investor flexibility for close-ended. Note: The workbook (pp. 112, 125, 391) supports PPM-specified lock-in/exit-load and the absence of unrestricted redemption before winding-up/tenure expiry for close-ended schemes.
